what: A turn detector decides when the speaker has finished so the agent can reply, and notices when they start talking again so the agent stops (barge-in). It combines voice activity detection (is anyone speaking?) with an end-of-turn signal from the transcript or a small model.
like: Like a good teacher who waits for a pupil to finish the sentence - and stops mid-word the moment the pupil puts a hand up.
why: Reply too early and you cut the learner off; too late and the tutor feels slow
Barge-in makes voice feel natural instead of walkie-talkie
It is often the biggest single slice of the voice latency budget

steps.d: Voice activity detection marks each short audio frame as speech or silence, cheaply and on every frame.
Speech-to-text streams partial words while the learner talks and a final transcript at the end of the turn.
End of turn fires after a short silence once the words look finished - AssemblyAI's model waits for terminal punctuation after a silence between a minimum and maximum threshold.
While the tutor is speaking, new speech from the learner triggers barge-in: stop text-to-speech and cancel the model stream at once.
Word timings from text-to-speech tell the agent the last word actually played; history is trimmed there so the tutor never assumes the learner heard the rest.

numbers.l: AssemblyAI default minimum turn silence (Universal-3.5 Pro streaming)
delay beyond which a reply starts to feel unnatural
LiveKit default transcript_timeout for manual turn control

choices.d: A fixed silence timer is simple but cuts people off mid-thought; a turn model or punctuation-aware endpointing waits through 'um' and reading out numbers.
VAD runs on every frame next to the audio (in the agent or browser); end of turn can come from the STT provider so you don't run a second model.
Ignore short 'mhm' and 'yeah' so they don't stop the tutor; require a minimum speech duration before counting an interruption.
Lower silence thresholds feel snappy but interrupt slow speakers; tune per audience (children and second-language speakers need longer).

instead.why: Many streaming STT models now return end-of-turn flags themselves
Push-to-talk avoids turn detection entirely, at the cost of naturalness

breaks.d: Silence threshold too short for someone thinking aloud.
breaks.see: Learners repeat themselves; many very short turns
breaks.fix: Longer max silence, punctuation-aware endpointing, per-learner tuning

breaks.d: Barge-in not wired to cancel TTS and the LLM stream.
breaks.fix: Cancel both streams on speech start

breaks.d: Any sound counts as an interruption.
breaks.fix: Minimum interruption duration and backchannel filtering

say: I measure from the learner's last word to the tutor's first audio, and turn detection is the first slice of that budget.
I use punctuation-aware end of turn from the STT plus VAD for barge-in, and filter backchannels so 'mhm' doesn't stop the tutor.
On an interruption I cancel TTS and the model, then trim the conversation to the words that were actually heard using TTS word timings.

followups.q: Why not just wait 2 seconds of silence?
followups.a: Two seconds feels broken in conversation; delays above roughly half a second already feel unnatural. Smart endpointing waits only when the sentence looks unfinished.
Recorded sessions replayed through the pipeline, counting false cut-offs and missed interruptions per hour, compared on every change.

today: Streaming STT models now ship their own end-of-turn detection, and agent frameworks like LiveKit Agents expose adaptive interruption handling with tunable endpointing delays.

check.q: The learner says 'my number is 0 7 9...' and pauses. What should a good turn detector do?
check.a: Keep listening until the number looks finished
check.why: Punctuation-aware endpointing holds the turn open through pauses in numbers and lists.

check.q: The learner interrupts. What must the agent do with its history?
check.a: Keep only the words actually played
d: Repeat the reply from the start
check.why: Word timings show what was heard; the rest never reached the learner.

check.q: The tutor stops every time the learner says 'mhm'. Fix?
check.a: Minimum interruption duration and backchannel filtering
